title: GTPL Hathway Ltd - 540602 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GTPL Hathway Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 19% YoY to INR11,464 million, but reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million (9.6% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 19% YoY and 12% QoQ, led by subscription revenue of INR3,455 million (up from INR3,024 million). Reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million, with management attributing the gap to ACT acquisition synergies not yet realised and to forex and transponder costs. Consolidated PAT was about negative INR0.5 million after INR75 million of one-off-type impacts (INR45 million forex loss, INR30 million transponder amortisation). The company closed the ACT Group cable TV acquisition on September 15, 2026 for INR35.55 crore, adding roughly 6 lakh digital TV subscribers, and it appointed a new broadband CEO.

segments.name: Digital TV (CATV)
segments.commentary: Digital cable TV base reached 11 million at September 30, 2026, with 1.5 million added in the quarter and 10.30 million paying subscribers; ACT contributed about 6 lakh of these. Business partner network is above 51,000.

segments.name: Broadband
segments.commentary: Active subscribers reached 1.07 million, up 10,000 QoQ; homepass stood at 6 million. ARPU was INR470 and average monthly data use was 436 GB per user (up 6% YoY).

segments.name: ACT Group cable business
segments.commentary: Acquired September 15, 2026 for INR35.55 crore cash across seven companies in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and Karnataka. Current operating margin is about 12%, with a target of 25-26% after integration.

segments.name: DL GTPL Cabnet
segments.commentary: Company is acquiring the remaining 74% stake (INR83.25 million) having held 26%. It has about 1.5 lakh CATV subscribers in Gujarat, Maharashtra and parts of MP.

guidance_outlook: Operational EBITDA margin expected to rise 150-250 bps by end FY27 from the 20-21% level, as ACT synergies and HITS delivery-cost benefits come through.
Digital TV net additions of 1.8-1.9 million for FY27 (1.65 million added so far this year).
Double-digit subscription revenue growth expected in both digital TV and broadband.
Medium term: digital TV base of 13-14 million and broadband base near 1.2 million in about three years; subscriber growth of 7-8% a year.
All integration of ACT expected by end FY27; existing network migration to HITS expected by December or January.
capex_capacity: Entire broadband network migrated to GPON, now a full FTTH network, per management.
Seven new transponders added; INR30 million amortisation impact booked in standalone financials this quarter.
No incremental capex or opex so far from higher data consumption; management said future increases would need only about 10% of the proportional cost.

Over 60% of existing digital TV network already moved to HITS (Headend in the Sky, launched November 2025); full conversion targeted by December or January, after which cable-dark, rural and semi-urban expansion starts.
demand_pricing: Broadband homepass-to-paying conversion rose from 13-14% earlier to 17-18%, with a target of about 20%.

Broadband net adds were about 10,000 QoQ versus the historical 25,000-40,000 per quarter; management attributed the slowdown to the FTTH migration and cleanup over the past 1-1.5 years and expects a return to about 20,000+ per month.
ARPU rise attributed to existing subscribers moving to higher plans.
Management says it is at parity with telcos on pricing and sees competition as healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What changes are expected in ARPU and margins in ACT markets versus established markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ACT is accretive; it has about 1.25 lakh primary subscribers at higher ARPU, and synergies will come over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did broadband net additions slow, and what is being done to revive them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the FTTH migration and cleanup over the last 1-1.5 years; it appointed Vivek Raina as broadband CEO three months ago, launched the TrueFiber brand, and targets 20,000+ monthly adds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACT integration status and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: ACT revenue is consolidated from September 15; current operating margin is about 12%, expected to reach 25-26% after integration into GTPL systems.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the digital TV subscriber growth came from ACT?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6 lakh of the 1.5 million quarterly additions came from ACT; management did not split the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not grow in line with revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisition synergies are not fully realised; operating EBITDA was about 20-21% versus 22% last year, and PAT was hit by forex and transponder costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drives ARPU growth and what is the mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Subscribers are moving to higher plans, lifting broadband ARPU to INR470; management expects double-digit subscription growth in both businesses.

risks_watch: Operational EBITDA margin fell to 20% from 22%; the 150-250 bps recovery depends on ACT synergies and HITS delivery-cost savings landing by year end.
Broadband net adds of about 10,000 in Q2 are well below the historical 25,000-40,000 per quarter; the recovery target depends on a new CEO and a new brand still at an early stage.
Forex loss of INR45 million and transponder amortisation of INR30 million weigh on PAT; management called these notional and expects them to ease over time.
Digital TV industry is facing technology and delivery-medium change; management flagged it as increasingly challenging for FY28.
Several ACT and DL GTPL Cabnet integration milestones were not quantified; management gave no ACT revenue or EBITDA split.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term subscriber and margin targets and on the new broadband team, but cautious on near-term profitability. It gave no ACT revenue or EBITDA split, and it repeatedly deferred integration benefits to the coming quarters and year end.
